payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. Sellers waiting here: LAV-01 from 6 P.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit, have you eaten? Look here — Taxi Blanco, very pretty card, twelve P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with your friends, eh?

Ay, hijo, ten? No. Six P for the Cava Baja, and that is my last word — if you say no, I close the box and we stay friends anyway. ¿Has comido? And listen: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, cariño.

—¡Dieciocho! Paco, ¿oyes a este señor? ¡Nos quiere hacer ricos y nosotros aquí regateando hacia abajo! Nada, nada, lo dicho es lo dicho: cuatro P y la Caña en la Cava Baja es tuya. Palabra de Nando. Pero rápido, que el equipo de al lado viene ya, ¿eh? ¿Trato?
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment, the sun is strong. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Barca del Estanque — a beautiful card, my favourite. For you, twelve P. My grandson started his album with this very same one.

¡Ay, qué simpático! Six is a little low for mi Taxi Blanco, hijo. Ten P, and we are friends. And look — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, take it, a gift from me. My nieto started his album with that one. Now, have you eaten something today?

"¡Amigo, amiga! Come, come — Paco's got the San Isidro right here, still warm from the case. Seventy-three pesos and she's yours."

"The squad next door's been circling it all morning, hermano, breathing on the glass. But we like your face better. Say the word, quick."

¡Primo, escucha! Hace un ratito pasó otro equipo y nos ofreció mucho más por este Ángel — Nando casi se lo vende. Pero tú eres paisano, y la familia primero. 57 P, cash en la mano, y nos vamos corriendo. Dilo ya, que cerramos el puesto.

¡Cincuenta, amigo, cincuenta! Paco: Casi, casi nos convences. Nando: Mira, el Alfonso XII no se ve dos veces en la vida. Paco: Sesenta y dos primas, y cerramos aquí mismo. Nando: ¡Sesenta y dos y te damos un abrazo gratis! Paco: ¡Venga, que el tren nos espera, hombre!

Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, the table does not bite. Have you eaten today? Look at this one — Vinilo de la Movida, very pretty, the colours still shine. For you, five P. Is a good card to start an album with, hijo.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the lucky face today, I see it! Look: Plaza del Dos de Mayo, beautiful card, the tourists weep for it. Four P and it is yours. Four! We leave before sunset, so... ¿sí?

"¡Cuarenta y cinco! Nando, sujétame, me caigo." — "Lo tengo, hermano." Amiga, la San Isidro no se regala, mírala, brilla como el sol de agosto. Por esa cara tan simpática: sesenta y seis pesos y nos damos la mano ahora mismo. Los de al lado vuelven en cinco minutos, ¿eh?

¡Ay, cariño, you bargain like my late husband! Seven is too little for mi Taxi Blanco. Nine P, and I am happy. Remember, swap your duplicates with your friends — a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Now go eat something, hijo, you look thin.

Ay, hijo, seven is a little thin for my old table. Ten P, like I said — and I will not move, because this card deserves it. Take it, finish your page, and come back Sunday with your duplicates. Did you eat something today? You look pale, cariño.

¡Cincuenta y tres! Paco: ¡Casi, hombre, casi! Nando: Cincuenta y ocho primas y el Alfonso XII sale volando contigo. Paco: Decide ya, que la policía... quiero decir, el taxi nos espera en la esquina. Nando: ¡Con el motor en marcha! Paco: ¡Cincuenta y ocho y un abrazo, amigo!

"¡Sin prisas dice! Nando, ¿oíste? La gente tranquila es la que más corre." — "Siempre, hermano."

Mira, amiga: sesenta y dos pesos. Mi abuela vendió su radio por menos y nunca se arrepintió. La mano está abierta, ¿la cerramos o se la lleva el de al lado?

¡Nando, listen to this man! He offers twenty — ¡qué corazón! But no, amigo, we are honest pícaros today. Four P, like we said, four, not one céntimo more from your pocket. Paco would blush. Take it, the sun is going down. ¿Sí? ¡Sí!
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Deal! Barca del Estanque for 9 P. Enjoy it, cariño.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
You again. La Rosaleda. Thirty-three P. That is the price, not the opening of a conversation.

payload.name: Don Ernesto
payload.teaser: «Gold is not shown. It is negotiated.»

payload.text: You move, I move. 33 P.

¡Hola, cariño! Sit, sit — have you eaten? Look, this one, El Titiritero, very handsome, no? For you, twelve P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

¡Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres! Nine P, like I said, and I even gave you the Plaza del Dos de Mayo for free, eh? Nine, and I wrap it nice for you. Then you go eat something warm, cariño — promise your abuela.

Ay, hijo, qué generosa eres, but no — five P and that is all. I will not take more from you, you need the coins for the bocadillo. Five P, the card is yours. And bring me your duplicates next Sunday, eh?

¡Cincuenta y cuatro! Paco: ¡Ay, que me da algo! Nando: Cincuenta y cinco, amigo, cincuenta y cinco y cerramos. Paco: Una prima, solo una, ¡por el honor de la maleta! Nando: ¡Y el abrazo sigue incluido! Paco: ¡Dale ya, que el taxista nos cobra por minuto!

"¡Cincuenta y uno! Nando, el taxi está esperando — la policía… digo, el taxi, hermano."

Amiga, cincuenta y ocho pesos. Última palabra, lo juro por mi abuela. No hay más baile. Si dice que no, cerramos la maleta y nos vamos con el motor en marcha. ¿Mano o adiós?

¡Amigo, basta, basta! Sixteen, eighteen, twenty — you throw money like confetti! Paco, hold his wrist. Four P, cuatro, that is the price, that was always the price. We are leaving, the van is running, Nando already has the card in your hand. ¡Sí? ¡Sí!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Another team offered us much more just now.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 11 P.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! ¡El Marqués! Paco, saca la caja— sí, la de terciopelo. Mira qué esquinas, limpias como espejo. Un coleccionista en Burgos lloró cuando la vendimos... bueno, casi. Para ti, hoy y sólo hoy: 73 P. Nos vamos en una hora, el tren no espera, ¿eh?

Ay, cariño, no, no — guarda ese dinero para comer. Five P, that is my last word, the very last. If you say no, I put her back in the box and no hard feelings, eh? And tonight, El Chato next door opens at half past nine — he likes honest traders like you.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.

¡Doce, ocho, cuatro — amigo, stop! Cuatro P. Last word, the final one, Paco swears on his mother. Refuse and we walk, card goes back in the case. The police— ¡the taxi! The taxi is waiting, motor running. Decide now, ahora mismo. ¿Sí? ¡Sí!
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one — Vinilo de la Movida, very pretty, my favourite from the old days. For you, 5 P. No hurry, hijo, look at everything you like first.
Buenas tardes, señor. How delightful — La Puerta de Alcalá, El Retiro's finest. I keep an album waiting for precisely that card. I offer you 151 P, and gladly. Shall we say it is done?

"¡Amigo, amiga! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. Look, look: Plaza del Dos de Mayo, four P, for you only." "The team at the next table was sniffing around it, eh? But we like your face better." "So — yes or yes?"
